sections.heading: Understanding & analysing emotions; dimensions of EI

blocks.text: **Emotional Intelligence (EI/EQ)** is the ability to **perceive, understand, manage and use emotions** — one's own and others'. Popularised by **Daniel Goleman**, it comprises five core dimensions and strongly predicts personal and professional success.

rows: Recognising one's own emotions and their effects.
Inner drive to achieve beyond external rewards.

items: **EI = self-awareness + self-regulation + motivation + empathy + social skills** (Goleman).
High EI aids leadership, decision-making and administrative service.

prelimsPointers: **Emotional Intelligence (EI/EQ)** — perceiving, understanding, managing & using emotions.
**Daniel Goleman's 5 dimensions** — self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills.
**Salovey & Mayer** originated the EI concept; Goleman popularised it.
The **first two** dimensions are personal competencies; the **last two** are social.
High EI correlates with better leadership & interpersonal effectiveness.
EI is **learnable**, unlike IQ which is relatively fixed.

glossary.definition: The ability to perceive, understand, manage and use emotions effectively.
Recognising one's own emotions and their impact — the first EI dimension.
The capacity to understand and share the feelings of others.

sections.heading: Coping with emotions; empathy; coping with stress

blocks.text: **Coping** is managing emotional and stressful situations constructively. Building **empathy** and adopting healthy **stress-coping strategies** (problem-focused and emotion-focused) are core life skills — vital for administrators dealing with pressure and people.

rows: Act on the stressor's cause (planning, problem-solving).
Manage the emotional response (relaxation, reframing, support).
Exercise, mindfulness, time management, social support.

items: **Problem-focused** = tackle the cause; **emotion-focused** = manage the feeling.
Empathy has cognitive, affective and compassionate components.

prelimsPointers: Two coping styles — **problem-focused** (change the situation) & **emotion-focused** (change the response).
**Empathy** = cognitive + affective + compassionate.
Healthy emotion regulation means **managing, not suppressing** feelings.
**Eustress** (positive) vs **distress** (negative) stress.
Stress-coping tools — **exercise, mindfulness, time management, social support**.
Emotional coping is a **learnable life skill** (WHO life-skills framework).

glossary.definition: Managing stress by acting on its underlying cause.
Managing stress by regulating the emotional response to it.
Positive, motivating stress, as opposed to harmful distress.

blocks.text: **Social intelligence** is the capacity to **understand and navigate social situations and relationships effectively**. It underlies **communication, teamwork, negotiation and leadership** — essential interpersonal skills for public service.

rows: Reading social cues, situations and others' feelings.
Communication, active listening, conflict resolution, teamwork.
Complements EI; key for leadership & administration.

items: **Active listening** and empathy underpin good interpersonal skills.

prelimsPointers: **Social intelligence** — ability to understand & manage social relationships (E.L. Thorndike coined the term).
Goleman splits it into **social awareness** & **social facility**.
Key interpersonal skills — **communication, active listening, empathy, conflict resolution, teamwork**.
Communication is **verbal + non-verbal (body language, tone)**.
Social intelligence **complements** emotional intelligence.
Vital for **leadership, negotiation and public administration**.

glossary.definition: The ability to understand and manage social situations and relationships.
Fully concentrating on, understanding and responding to a speaker.
Conveying meaning through body language, tone and expression rather than words.

sections.heading: Decision making, critical thinking & problem solving

blocks.text: **Decision-making, critical thinking and problem-solving** are interlinked cognitive skills for choosing the best course of action. They follow a rational process of **defining the problem, generating and evaluating options, and choosing/implementing a solution**.

rows: Define problem → gather info → list alternatives → evaluate → decide → implement → review.
Objective analysis, questioning assumptions, avoiding bias/fallacies.
Systematic approach to overcome an obstacle to a goal.
Rational, intuitive, ethical; individual vs group.

items: Follow the **rational decision cycle**: define → options → evaluate → decide → review.
**Critical thinking** guards against cognitive biases and logical fallacies.

prelimsPointers: Rational decision cycle — **define → gather info → alternatives → evaluate → decide → implement → review**.
**Critical thinking** = objective, reasoned analysis free of bias.
Common biases — **confirmation, anchoring, groupthink, sunk-cost**.
Decision types — **rational, intuitive, ethical; individual vs group**.
**SWOT** (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) aids decisions.
Problem-solving and decision-making are core administrative competencies.

glossary.definition: Objective, reasoned analysis of information to form a judgement, free of bias.
The tendency to favour information confirming one's existing beliefs.
The process of selecting the best course of action among alternatives.

blocks.text: **Personality** is the characteristic pattern of thoughts, feelings and behaviours that makes a person unique. It is assessed through **trait theories (Big Five), type theories, and psychometric tests** — relevant to self-awareness and administrative aptitude.

rows: **Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism** — the leading trait model.
Self-report inventories, projective tests (Rorschach, TAT), interviews.

items: **Big Five = OCEAN** — the most validated personality model.
**Projective tests** (Rorschach inkblot, TAT) tap unconscious traits.

prelimsPointers: **Big Five (OCEAN)** — Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism.
**MBTI (Myers-Briggs)** — 16 personality types (based on Jung).
**Projective tests** — **Rorschach (inkblot), TAT (Thematic Apperception Test)**.
**Trait theories** treat personality as continuous dimensions; **type theories** as categories.
Personality is shaped by **heredity + environment**.
Self-report **inventories** are common psychometric tools.

glossary.definition: The five-factor personality model: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism.
A personality assessment (e.g. Rorschach) revealing unconscious traits via ambiguous stimuli.
The view that personality consists of measurable continuous dimensions (traits).
